newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates flat to lower as liquidity eyed.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates flat to lower as liquidity eyed.

text.p: Interbank rates were flat to lower as the market eyed the liquidity situation after the recent inflow of funds which has depressed rates, dealers said.
They said while short-term rates were soft, the long-term rates were more stable. The central bank was not expected to make drastic moves to depress rates further so soon.
"Money rates can't come down too much. It would be too drastic," said a Malaysian bank dealer.
The fall in rates started on Monday after heavy lending by big local banks in the one-month segment, said to be on behalf of the central bank. The big banks were reticent so far, dealers said.
No confirmation was available from Bank Negara Malaysia as it does not comment on its market intervention operations.
The one-, two- and three-week money were trading at 7.50/80 percent against 8.0/9.0 on Tuesday, dealers said.
Activity was again centered on the one-month money on Wednesday. The rate was at 8.0 percent against 7.5/8.0.
Three month money was at 7.50/80 percent from 7.50/8.0.
"One-month is very well traded. Most were done at 8.0 percent," said another dealer.
The overnight interbank rate which ended steady at 8.8/9.0 percent was expected to ease in the next few days, they said.
"By week's end it should come off," the dealer said.
In the futures market, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) contracts were all lower.
The June 1997 contract was down four basis points to 92.46, or an implied yield of 7.54 percent.
September 1997 contract was down two points to 92.58, or 7.42 percent and December was down two to 92.60, or 7.40 percent.
